channel.title: France 24 - International breaking news, top stories and headlines
channel.description: Breaking news and world news from France 24 on Business, Sports, Culture. Video news. News from the US, Europe, Asia Pacific, Africa, Middle East, America

item.title: Wildfires kill 12 in Algeria as severe heatwave sweeps North Africa
item.description: Twelve people died and dozens were injured as wildfires tore through northern Algeria on Wednesday, with authorities battling more than 150 blazes amid a scorching heatwave sweeping across North Africa. Six of the 54 injured were in critical condition and receiving intensive care.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: FDA approves new drug Rasonque to treat advanced pancreatic cancer
item.description: The US FDA on Wednesday approved Revolution Medicines' Rasonque for advanced pancreatic cancer, opening a new treatment option for patients with metastatic disease. A large trial found the once-daily pill doubled survival rates, offering fresh hope for people who have exhausted other treatments.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: South-Africa kingpin and the corruption commission
item.description: In tonight's programme, a three-day testimony of an alleged underworld kingpin exposed how deep the link between alleged criminals and high profile police officers is in South Africa. Also, in Tunisia grieving families lay their lost youth, all victims of a boat that went down in the Mediterranean Sea over the weekend. And finally in an era of mass production and electric machines, a young Kenyan fashion designer is taking a slower approach.
item.dc:creator: Georja CALVIN-SMITH

item.title: Navigation, jurisdiction, costs: Iran, Oman attempt to hammer out Hormuz deal
item.description: Iran and Oman are holding talks to try to reach an interim agreement for a controlled resumption of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. The two countries have discussed a framework for a “temporary corridor” for shipping, according to a joint statement by the Iranian and Omani foreign ministries. But the plan faces several hurdles.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Tim Curry, star of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' and 'It', dies at 80
item.description: Tim Curry, the British character actor who created a gallery of flamboyant villains for stage and screen, most famously Dr. Frank-N-Furter in the 1975 cult classic "The Rocky Horror Picture Show", has died at the age of 80, his manager said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Exclusive: French astronaut Sophie Adenot recounts her ‘miracle’ mission from orbiting ISS
item.description: In an exclusive interview with FRANCE 24 and RFI from the International Space Station, French astronaut Sophie Adenot hailed a "mission accomplished" after two spacewalks to replace a faulty antenna and called the operation "a miracle", given the mechanical setbacks. She also described the "blatant" signs of climate change she has seen from orbit.
item.dc:creator: Sylvain ROUSSEAU

item.title: Space: Sophie Adenot recounts her two spacewalks
item.description:
🇫🇷 👩‍🚀 Sophie Adenot, the first French woman to conduct a spacewalk and the second female French astronaut to go to space, gave an exclusive interview to #FRANCE24 and #RFI from the International Space Station.
In conversation with our journalists, she reflected on the feeling of leaping into the vast unknown of space for the first time.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Syria: Why is the dissolution of the Kurdish forces significant?
item.description: The Syrian Kurdish Forces announced their dissolution on August 25, in what is considered a significant step for Syria. FRANCE 24's Andrew Hilliar tells us why.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Dolly Parton: Buckingham Palace guards play musical tribute
item.description: Britain’s royal family posted a video on social media Wednesday of the band of the Buckingham Palace guards playing Dolly Parton’s “9 to 5”, in tribute to the American country music legend who passed away Tuesday aged 80.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: ‘Shockwaves throughout the country’ following ‘gruesome’ killings in Haitian mountain retreat
item.description: Genie Godula is pleased to welcome journalist Harold Isaac on the ground in Haiti's capital, Port-au-Prince. He says what we are witnessing in Haiti is not simply another episode of gang violence, but a profound challenge to the authority of the state at a moment when the country is attempting to return to electoral politics. With armed groups controlling roughly 80 percent of Port-au-Prince, the capital is effectively under siege, while the circulation of people, goods and services increasingly requires some form of negotiation with gang power. The attack in Kenscoff is especially significant because of its proximity to some of the country’s most affluent areas. This as authorities seek to organize Haiti’s first elections in a decade, against a backdrop of arms smuggling, institutional fragility and an unresolved political transition.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Russia: CIA director visits Moscow
item.description: CIA director John Ratcliffe held talks with Russian intelligence services in Moscow, the Kremlin confirmed Wednesday, the first know visit by a US spy chief to the Russian capital since 2021. It is not known what Ratcliffe discussed with his Russian counterparts, but the talks come as ‌the war in Ukraine is escalating and as ⁠efforts to reach a lasting peace between the US and Iran have stalled.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Tornado wreaks havoc in village in southwestern France
item.description: A tornado swept through a village in the Aude ​region of southwestern France late on Monday, destroying homes and injuring dozens, authorities said, describing it as a rare and traumatic event. Around 300 of the 500 houses in the ​village of ‌Pomas have been damaged, officials said, adding that 100 of ⁠the damaged ones may no longer be safe to live in.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Hundreds missing in Nepal catastrophic flash floods
item.description: Massive flash floods in Nepal on Wednesday killed at least 22 people and left hundreds of tourists, workers and others missing after sweeping through communities and bringing travel in parts of the Himalayan country to a halt. China's government across the northern border also launched search and rescue efforts, with major casualties in the border area of Gyirong, state broadcaster CCTV reported. No toll was immediately reported.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: From tariffs to French: Trump’s trade war with Canada takes a cultural turn
item.description: A trade war between Canada and the United States is escalating. Canada has announced retaliatory tariffs ranging from 15% to 50% on about $20 billion worth of American goods, after new 50% US tariffs on Canadian products took effect Saturday. But the tit-for-tat over goods has also taken on a cultural and linguistic dimension.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Dolly Parton, queen of country music, dies at 80
item.description: Dolly Parton was around six when she wrote her first song: "Little Tiny Tasseltop," an ⁠ode to her corncob doll with ​corn-silk hair. Her mother stored it preciously in a shoebox. Parton never stopped making music after that. The irrepressible country music singer, songwriter and actress whose charisma, heartfelt lyrics and ​business acumen captured the public's imagination for nearly six decades, died on Tuesday aged 80, her family said in a statement.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'Major casualties': Devastating floods wash away villages on Nepal-Tibet border
item.description: Massive flooding near the border with Tibet killed dozens in Nepal on Wednesday. Hundreds of people were still out of contact hours after the disaster hit. A torrent of mud and debris burst from the banks of a river between China and Nepal, burying buildings and triggering a frantic search for survivors. FRANCE 24's Sarah Jacob reports from New Delhi, India.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Turkey says dissolution of Kurdish-led group crucial for Syrian stability
item.description: Turkey on Wednesday said the dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) marked a key step towards strengthening state authority and achieving lasting stability in Syria. Turkey has long regarded the SDF as an extension of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers' Party (PKK), which waged an insurgency against the Turkish state for decades. FRANCE 24's Jasper Mortimer reports from Ankara, Turkey.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Gang attack in Haiti: Anger mounts over police failures
item.description: At least 47 people were killed and more than 50 others kidnapped after armed men attacked a once-peaceful community near Haiti’s capital earlier this week, the United Nations said Tuesday. It is believed to be one of the largest mass kidnappings in Haiti in recent years, and one gang leader is threatening to kill the hostages if authorities kill any gang members as they try to secure the community nestled in the hills above Port-au-Prince. Sunday’s attack on Kenscoff pierced the belief that security in the troubled Caribbean country was improving. Journalist Harold Isaac reports from Port-au-Prince, Haiti.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: 'In Ceuta, they are eating the cats': Fake images and a persistent rumour
item.description: Cats “massacred” in the Spanish enclave of Ceuta? Three weeks after thousands of migrants crossed the border into Ceuta, Spanish websites and social media users are claiming that the migrants who have stayed are killing cats. But all of the dead cat photos that have been shared so far are either fake or have been taken out of context. Our team spoke to a local cat rescue organisation, which also confirmed that this is a rumour.
item.dc:creator: The FRANCE 24 Observers

item.title: Meta reaches $17 billion settlement with US states over social media harm to teens
item.description: Meta Platforms on Wednesday agreed to pay $17 billion to settle claims, filed by 47 US states, that the company designed Facebook and Instagram to deliberately make teens addicted to their products while deceiving the public, according to state attorneys general. The company agreed to add child-safety measures as part of the settlement.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Nepal: Hundreds reported missing after deadly flash floods
item.description: Entire roads and villages have been engulfed in mud after flash floods struck a border crossing between Tibet and Nepal. Hundreds are reported missing, including over 300 tourists. Flood alerts have also been issued in the Indian states of Bihar and Uttar Pradesh.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Panama and El Salvador declare emergency over El Nino-fuelled drought
item.description: Panama and El Salvador have become the latest countries along with Honduras to declare an emergency over El Nino, which has already forced a reduction in shipping through the Panama Canal. All three countries broke their monthly temperature records in both June and July, exacerbating famine concerns.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: Deadly flash floods near Nepal-Tibet border raze villages, leave hundreds missing
item.description: Massive flash floods that swept through the Himalayan border regions of Nepal and Tibet on Wednesday killed at least 160 people and destroyed villages and infrastructure, officials said. Hundreds are still missing, including foreign tourists and pilgrims from neighbouring India, as authorities race to send humanitarian assistance to affected communities.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE 24

item.title: US country music legend Dolly Parton dies, aged 80
item.description: Dolly Parton was one of the rare celebrities that transcended divides in the United States. The country music legend and actress died, aged 80, on August 25.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24
